Internode intervals of a pure-birth process with lineage-dependent rates

Source: R/simulate.R
intervals_lineage_rate.Rd

With k lineages each splits at rate k^c, so the interval with k lineages is Exp(k^(1 + c)). c = 0 is Yule; c < 0 slows diversification as lineages accumulate (gamma < 0); c > 0 accelerates it (gamma > 0). The final interval (n lineages, up to the present) is drawn from the same law.

Usage

intervals_lineage_rate(n, c = 0, rate = NULL)

Arguments

n

Number of tips, a single integer of at least 2.

c

Lineage dependence of the split rate, a single finite number.

rate

NULL (the default), to use c, or a vectorized function of the number of lineages k that returns the per-lineage split rate. It must return n - 1 positive, finite values for k = 2, ..., n, and cannot be combined with a c other than 0.

Value

Intervals g_2, ..., g_n (length n - 1), scaled to sum 1.

Details

Any other dependence on the number of lineages can be given with rate, a function of k that returns the per-lineage split rate; the interval with k lineages is then Exp(k * rate(k)), and c is the special case rate = function(k) k^c. Only the shape of rate matters: the intervals are rescaled, so multiplying it by a constant does not change the tree. As with c, the shape of rate describes the lineage-through-time curve and does not identify the mechanism behind it (Pannetier et al. 2021). calibrate_shape(), shape_params() and sim_tree_target() work with c only; with rate, the calibration is left to the user.

References

Pannetier, T., Martinez, C., Bunnefeld, L., & Etienne, R. S. (2021). Branching patterns in phylogenies cannot distinguish diversity-dependent diversification from time-dependent diversification. Evolution, 75, 25–38. doi:10.1111/evo.14124

Pybus, O. G., & Harvey, P. H. (2000). Testing macro-evolutionary models using incomplete molecular phylogenies. Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 267, 2267–2272. doi:10.1098/rspb.2000.1278

Examples

set.seed(1)
intervals_lineage_rate(10, c = -1)
#> [1] 0.09121461 0.14272468 0.01759918 0.01688517 0.05267053 0.34966867 0.14851261
#> [8] 0.06518557 0.11553897
# logistic slowdown towards a carrying capacity K > n
intervals_lineage_rate(10, rate = function(k) 1 - k / 12)
#> [1] 0.01812595 0.12698669 0.05870831 0.08717482 0.30295889 0.07428034 0.07975727
#> [8] 0.17129897 0.08070879
# the rate drops once there are more than 5 lineages
intervals_lineage_rate(10, rate = function(k) ifelse(k <= 5, 1, 0.1))
#> [1] 0.05331123 0.06207473 0.18706249 0.04062533 0.15512381 0.25581133 0.04195830
#> [8] 0.02089944 0.18313334
